basics.name: Jordan Hale
basics.label: Design Engineer
basics.summary:
Design engineer who treats stylesheets as a public interface. I build design systems, documentation sites, and the quiet HTML underneath them — the kind of markup a parser and a person can both read.

I want tools that stay out of the way: one semantic skeleton, many skins, no framework tax on the page a hiring manager opens.

work.name: Acme Studio
work.summary: Lead the shared component contract used across product teams.
highlights: Lead the shared component contract used by six product teams; cut visual regressions in half by locking class names and token names as an API.
Shipped the design-system documentation site as static HTML + one CSS file per theme, including a dark theme and a high-contrast theme.
Mentored designers writing production CSS: cascade layers, logical properties, and what not to hide from assistive tech.

work.name: Lumen Civic
highlights: Redesigned the public-records request flow; completion rate rose from 41% to 73% without adding a JavaScript framework to the citizen-facing pages.
Wrote the first content model for agendas and minutes so the same HTML could print, archive, and screen-read.
Partnered with engineering on an Elm admin and a boring HTML front door.

work.name: Atlas Press
highlights: Designed and implemented catalog and essay templates as semantic articles with print stylesheets.
Produced type specimens and CSS themes for a seasonal design-showcase series.

volunteer.summary: Monthly type and CSS workshops for early-career designers.
highlights: Ran a twelve-week semantic HTML studio for civic-tech volunteers.

courses: Thesis: Responsive typography and presentational markup

awards.title: CSS Design Awards — Site of the Day

publications.name: The stylesheet is a public API
publications.summary: On locking class names so themes and tools can share one HTML tree.

references.name: Sam Okonkwo
references.reference: Jordan treats markup as a contract. Our design system survived six product teams because they refused to let class names drift.

projects.name: Type Garden
projects.description: A fixed article skeleton restyled by invited typographers.
highlights: Thirty submitted stylesheets, one HTML file, no preprocessor in the published artifacts.
Documented a class contract so late themes could ship without touching markup.

projects.name: Minutes, Plain
projects.description: City-council minutes as readable HTML with an ATS-safe export.
highlights: Plain-language templates adopted by two neighboring municipalities.
